$comment: WHY release-type 'simple': this repository ships DOCKER IMAGES, not npm
packages. The 'node' release type would rewrite package.json versions and
expect a publish step that does not exist here. 'simple' tracks the
version in .release-please-manifest.json, writes the changelog, tags, and
stops -- which is exactly the contract the release workflow needs before
it builds and pushes to ghcr.io.
WHY the linked-versions plugin: contracts and web are a matched pair. The
web app is built against a specific ABI, so shipping web 1.3.0 against
contracts 1.1.0 is a support question nobody wants to answer. Linking
them means one version number moves everything, and the tags on all three
WHY separate-pull-requests is false: one release PR is one human review
and one merge, which produces one coherent set of image tags.
$comment-tags: include-component-in-tag defaults to true here so the workspace releases
get distinct tags (contracts-v1.1.0, web-v1.1.0). The ROOT overrides it to
false so the headline tag stays a bare v1.1.0. Without that override all
three components would try to create the same tag and the release would
pull-request-header: Merging this PR tags the release and builds the ghcr.io images.

..$comment: The root component. Its version is what the image tags carry, so it is the one users see. Tag is a bare vX.Y.Z.

contracts.$comment: Solidity + Hardhat workspace. Its own changelog, but never its own version -- see linked-versions below.

web.$comment: Vite frontend workspace. Built against the contracts ABI, hence linked.

plugins.$comment: Forces every listed component onto one version number, chosen by the largest bump any of them earned. 'groupName' labels the combined release PR.
